drafts.rationale: EV-O-A04 restates that each job is delivered to a worker for execution, matching the known executor claim.
EV-O-A04 restates an execution as one delivery ending in success, failure or timeout.
EV-O-A04 repeats that each job begins with one initial execution.
EV-O-A04 restates the cap of up to three retry executions after an unsuccessful initial execution.
EV-O-A04 restates that no further execution may be started after the third unsuccessful retry.
EV-O-A04 still treats the initial execution as additional to the three permitted retries.
EV-O-B04 restates the exact five-second wait from the end of a failed attempt before a retry.
EV-O-B04 restates that the retry wait must not vary with attempt number.
EV-O-C04 restates the per-execution time limit as half a minute, which is thirty seconds.
EV-O-C04 restates that an execution must be stopped when the time limit is reached.
EV-O-C04 restates that a timed-out execution is a failed attempt and the retry rules apply.
EV-O-D04 restates that further deliveries of an active job id must be ignored.
EV-O-D04 restates that ignoring a duplicate delivery must not change active job state.
EV-O-E04 restates that deliveries may carry an idempotency key chosen by the producer.
EV-O-E04 restates twenty-four-hour retention of each idempotency key after it is first seen.
EV-O-E04 restates that after retention the key may be forgotten and a later same-key delivery is treated as new.
EV-O-F04 restates that delivery grants the receiving worker a lease that keeps other workers away.
EV-O-F04 restates that a worker lease lasts sixty seconds from delivery.
EV-O-F04 restates that expiry without renewal or release makes the job available to other workers.
EV-O-G04 restates that a worker may renew its lease every thirty seconds while work is progressing.
EV-O-G04 restates that a renewal extends the lease by the full lease duration from the moment of renewal.
EV-O-H04 restates that producers and operators may cancel jobs.
EV-O-H04 restates that after cancellation no future execution attempt of that job may be started.
EV-O-H04 restates that cancellation must not interrupt an already running attempt.
EV-O-I04 restates automatic movement to the dead-letter queue after the final unsuccessful attempt.
EV-O-I04 restates that a dead-lettered job must not be executed again unless explicitly resubmitted.
EV-O-J04 restates that three dead-letter events for the same tenant within one hour raise an operator escalation.
EV-O-J04 restates that the one-hour window is measured from the first of the three events.
EV-O-K04 restates that ordering is promised only where it does not serialise the whole service.
EV-O-K04 restates FIFO execution order only among jobs in the same queue partition.
EV-O-K04 restates that no ordering guarantee is made between jobs in different partitions.
EV-O-L04 restates that each job state change is recorded as an audit event.
EV-O-L04 restates that audit events must be retained for thirty days after they are recorded.
EV-O-L04 restates that an audit event may be deleted after thirty days.

propositions.statement: Orion delivers each job to a worker for execution.
An execution is one delivery that ends in success, failure or timeout.
Each job begins with one initial execution.
Executions per job are capped: if the initial execution does not succeed, the worker may perform up to three retry executions.
When the third retry has ended without success, no further execution of that job may be started.
The initial execution is additional to the three permitted retry executions.
Before every retry attempt the worker must wait exactly five seconds from the end of the failed attempt.
The retry wait must not be shortened or lengthened based on the attempt number.
An individual execution may run for no longer than half a minute (thirty seconds).
When the execution time limit is reached the execution must be stopped.
An execution stopped at the time limit must be recorded as a failed attempt and the retry rules take over.
While a job with a given job id is active, any further delivery carrying the same job id must be ignored and the job is not run twice.
Ignoring a duplicate delivery must not change the state of the active job.
Deliveries may carry a producer-chosen idempotency key.
Orion must retain each idempotency key for twenty-four hours after it is first seen so repeats can be recognised.
After the retention period the key may be forgotten and a later delivery with the same key is treated as new.
Delivering a job to a worker grants that worker a lease that marks the job as in hand and keeps other workers away from it.
A worker lease must last sixty seconds from the moment the job is delivered to the worker.
When the lease expires without renewal or release, the job must become available to other workers.
A worker may renew its lease every thirty seconds while work on the job is progressing.
A renewal must extend the lease by the full lease duration from the moment of renewal.
Producers and operators can cancel jobs.
After a job is cancelled, no future execution attempt of that job may be started.
Cancellation must not interrupt an already running execution attempt; that attempt runs to its own completion, failure or timeout.
After the final unsuccessful execution attempt, Orion must automatically move the job to the dead-letter queue.
A job in the dead-letter queue must not be executed again unless explicitly resubmitted.
When three dead-letter events occur for the same tenant within one hour, Orion must raise an operator escalation.
The one-hour escalation window must be measured from the first of the three events.
Orion promises order only where doing so does not serialise the whole service.
First-in-first-out execution order must be guaranteed only among jobs in the same queue partition.
No ordering guarantee is made between jobs in different partitions.
Each job state change produces an audit event.
Audit events must be retained for thirty days after they are recorded.
After thirty days an audit event may be deleted.

sentences_to_account.text: Orion delivers each job to a worker for execution.
One delivery that ends in success, failure or timeout is an execution.
Because some jobs can never succeed, the number of executions per job is capped.
Each job begins with one initial execution.
If the initial execution does not succeed, the worker may perform up to three retry executions of that job.
When the third retry has ended without success, no further execution of that job may be started.
Job Q-31 fails on its initial execution and on three retries.
Q-31 is not executed a fifth time.
Once an execution has failed, Orion pauses before delivering the job again so that a transient fault downstream has a chance to clear.
Before every retry attempt the worker must wait exactly five seconds, measured from the end of the failed attempt.
The wait must not be shortened or lengthened based on the attempt number.
Q-31's initial execution fails at 08:14:10; the first retry starts no earlier than 08:14:15.
Each later retry likewise starts no earlier than five seconds after the preceding failure.
Workers can stall.
To keep a stalled worker from holding a job forever, every execution is subject to a time limit, after which the execution is treated as a failure and the retry rules take over.
An individual execution may run for no longer than half a minute; when that limit is reached the execution must be stopped.
An execution stopped at the limit must be recorded as a failed attempt.
Job Q-31's retry starts at 08:15:00 and is still running at 08:15:30; Orion stops it and records a failure.
A producer that times out may send the same job again.
Orion recognises the repeat by job id and does not run the job twice.
While a job with a given job id is active, any further delivery carrying the same job id must be ignored.
Ignoring a duplicate delivery must not change the state of the active job.
Q-52 is delivered at 11:00 and again at 11:02 while still active; the second delivery is dropped and Q-52 is unaffected.
Deliveries may carry a producer-chosen idempotency key.
Orion keeps recent keys so repeats can be recognised.
Orion must retain each idempotency key for twenty-four hours after it is first seen.
After the retention period the key may be forgotten and a later delivery with the same key is treated as new.
Key IK-77 first appears on Thursday at 13:00; it is recognised at Thursday 23:00 and forgotten by Friday 14:00.
Delivering a job to a worker grants that worker a lease.
The lease tells Orion the job is in hand and keeps other workers away from it.
A worker lease must last sixty seconds from the moment the job is delivered to the worker.
When the lease expires without renewal or release, the job must become available to other workers.
Worker W-2 receives Q-40 at 09:30:00 and goes silent.
At 09:31:00 the lease lapses and Q-40 can be handed to W-5.
A worker that is still making progress renews its lease so that the job is not reassigned underneath it.
A worker may renew its lease every thirty seconds while work on the job is progressing.
A renewal must extend the lease by the full lease duration from the moment of renewal.
W-2 renews Q-40's sixty-second lease at 09:30:30; the lease now ends at 09:31:30.
Producers and operators can cancel jobs.
Cancellation tells Orion to stop investing in the job; it does not reach into a worker and abort work already under way.
After a job is cancelled, no future execution attempt of that job may be started.
Cancellation must not interrupt an execution attempt that is already running; that attempt runs to its own completion, failure or timeout.
Q-40 is cancelled while its second execution is running.
That execution finishes on its own terms and no further execution follows.
A job that has spent its attempt budget without succeeding is parked for inspection rather than left blocking the queue.
After the final unsuccessful execution attempt, Orion must automatically move the job to the dead-letter queue.
A job in the dead-letter queue must not be executed again unless explicitly resubmitted.
Q-31 exhausts its attempts at 08:20; Orion places it in the dead-letter queue at 08:20 with no operator action.
Many dead-letter events for one tenant in a short time usually mean something systemic.
Orion raises an escalation when that pattern appears.
When three dead-letter events occur for the same tenant within one hour, Orion must raise an operator escalation.
The one-hour window must be measured from the first of the three events.
Tenant T-7 produces dead-letter events at 08:20, 08:45 and 09:10; the third falls within an hour of the first, so an escalation is raised.
Some producers rely on enqueue order.
Orion promises order only where doing so does not serialise the whole service.
First-in-first-out execution order must be guaranteed only among jobs in the same queue partition.
No ordering guarantee is made between jobs in different partitions.
Q-60 then Q-61 are enqueued into partition P-1; Q-60 starts first.
Q-62 in P-2 has no ordering relation to either.
Each job state change produces an audit event used for investigations and tenant reports.
Audit events are kept for a bounded period.
Audit events must be retained for thirty days after they are recorded.
After thirty days an audit event may be deleted.
An audit event written on 2 June may be removed on or after 2 July.
